# Provenance

Vendored copy of [coder/ghostty-web](https://github.com/coder/ghostty-web), MIT licence, Copyright (c) 2025 Coder (see [LICENSE](LICENSE)). See [ADR 041](../../../../docs/adrs/041.client.libghostty-vt.md).

- **Upstream commit:** `1858a5947767a3e1c9e98dbf53b2ff87fedb2aab` (2026-06-28), the `gitHead` of npm `ghostty-web@0.4.0-next.20.g1858a59`.
- **TypeScript:** every non-test file under upstream `lib/` (including `addons/` and `providers/`), copied byte for byte. Upstream's tests (`*.test.ts`, `test-helpers.ts`) and its happy-dom preload were not copied.
- **`ghostty-vt.wasm`:** copied byte for byte from the npm package. Built by Coder from Ghostty `5714ed07a1012573261b7b7e3ed2add9c1504496` plus upstream `patches/ghostty-wasm-api.patch`, so it is Ghostty code under Ghostty's MIT licence, Copyright (c) 2024 Mitchell Hashimoto, Ghostty contributors ([LICENSE.ghostty](LICENSE.ghostty), copied from Ghostty at that commit), plus Coder's MIT-licensed patch. Size and sha256 are in [ghostty-vt.wasm.json](ghostty-vt.wasm.json) and checked by `src/client/vendor/ghostty-web.test.ts`.

`bun run build` writes both notices to `dist/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES`.

webtty edits to these files are tracked in git from the commit that added them; diff against that commit to see them.

## Local changes

- `terminal.ts`: the mouse cursor is the default arrow instead of the `text` I-beam when not over a link (`mouseCursorFor`); `pointer` over links is unchanged.
- `input-handler.ts`: mouse motion with no button held is reported as button 35 instead of 32, the left-drag code (`mouseMotionButton`), a release outside the terminal no longer leaves a button held, and motion is reported once per cell instead of per `mousemove` (`isNewMouseCell`).
- `renderer.ts`: the canvas is drawn at the device pixel ratio rounded up to a whole number (`wholeDevicePixelRatio`), backing-store sizes are rounded the same way in `resize()` and `render()`, ratio changes are followed through a re-armed resolution media query (`watchDevicePixelRatio`), and `devicePixelRatio` is a public read-only getter.
- `renderer.ts`: `render()` reads the viewport once per frame through `getViewport` and serves screen rows, including the cursor cell, as slices of that snapshot (`frameLines`) instead of calling `getLine` per row, which copied and parsed the whole viewport each time.
- `terminal.ts`: `write()` applies DECSCUSR (`scanDecscusr`, `decscusrShape`) as an app cursor shape over the configured `cursorStyle` / `cursorBlink`, which Ps 0 and `reset()` restore; `renderer.ts`: a style or blink change repaints the cursor row on the next frame so the old shape does not stay under the new one.
- `terminal.ts`, `interfaces.ts`: when the app tracks the mouse, `handleWheel` sends SGR scroll buttons 64/65 at the cell under the pointer on either screen instead of arrow keys or a viewport scroll, counting pixel deltas one tick per cell height and line/page deltas one tick times the new `mouseScrollSpeed` option (`wheelTicks`, `wheelSgr`, now in `wheel.ts`).
- `addons/fit.ts`: `proposeDimensions` no longer subtracts a fixed 15 px scrollbar reserve (the scrollbar is an overlay inside the canvas); the grid math is the pure `fitDimensions`.
- `terminal.ts`: focus that lands on the contenteditable container (padding clicks, tab focus, `focus()`, a window regaining focus) is sent to the textarea, and the render loop anchors the textarea at the cursor cell, one cell high (`cursorCellOffset`, public `getCursorCellOffset`), so IME text never lands in the container and OS panels follow the cursor.
- `ghostty.ts`, `types.ts`, `index.ts`: a second engine on Ghostty's official libghostty-vt wasm (ADR 042). `GhosttyTerminal` and `KeyEncoder` are interfaces implemented by the Coder engine (`CoderTerminal`, the former `GhosttyTerminal` class) and the official engine (`OfficialTerminal`, `OfficialGhostty`); `Ghostty.load(path, engine)` returns either. The interface adds `setCellPixelSize`, the pixel arguments of `resize`, `setViewportOffset` (official only), `readEffects` and `answersSizeQueries`, which are no-ops or empty on the Coder engine. `GhosttyTerminalConfig` gains `colorsSet`, which the Coder engine ignores. The official engine drops the kitty keyboard query reply (`CSI ? flags u`), since keys are never encoded with the kitty flags.
- `terminal.ts`, `renderer.ts`: the client runs either engine (ADR 042). `open()`, `resize()`, `reset()` and the new `syncCellPixelSize()` pass the device-pixel cell size (`deviceCellPixels`) to the engine; replies are drained after `write`, after a resize or pixel-size change and after each frame's render; on the official engine bell and title come from `readEffects` instead of the stream scan; `parseColorToHex`, which returned 0 for an unset colour and for `#000000` alike, is replaced by `parseColor`, which returns undefined for unset or invalid colours, and `buildWasmConfig` fills `colorsSet` from it; `render()` calls the buffer's optional `setViewportOffset(viewportY)` first.
- `renderer.ts`, `terminal.ts`: a grapheme cell is drawn from the row the line came from. `renderCellText` looked graphemes up with `getGraphemeString(canvasRow, col)`, which reads a screen row, so while scrolled a scrollback grapheme was drawn as whatever sat at that column of the screen row (a stray letter, or `\u0000` as a missing-glyph box on the Coder engine). `renderLine` now takes a grapheme lookup: scrollback rows use the new `IScrollbackProvider.getScrollbackGraphemeString`, scrolled screen rows use their screen row.
- `renderer.ts`, `terminal.ts`, `ghostty.ts`: `render()` repaints only the canvas rows that changed, exactly as a full redraw leaves them (`repaintRows`: a run of rows plus the row below, drawn unclipped on a scratch canvas, then the run's rows copied in), instead of every row on a viewport move and on every frame while scrolled. A whole-line viewport move with nothing else changed copies the rows still in view with one `drawImage` of the canvas onto itself (`shiftRows`) and draws only the rows that came into view (ADR 043). The cursor row is repainted only when the drawn cursor changes, and the cursor is not drawn again over an unchanged one (a translucent cursor colour would build up), a `contextrestored` canvas is resized and repainted in full, a frame that drops the scrollbar repaints every row, theme, font and ratio changes repaint every row, and resize and font changes render with the current scrollbar opacity. The official engine reports its real dirty state while scrolled.
- `renderer.ts`, `terminal.ts`, `selection-manager.ts`: overscan for pixel-smooth scroll (ADR 043 step 2). The renderer draws on a canvas of its own, inserted before the terminal's canvas element, absolutely positioned at its static position and ignoring the mouse; the element keeps the layout box and the mouse events and draws nothing. That canvas holds `overscan` rows (`RendererOptions.overscan`, default `DEFAULT_OVERSCAN`) above and below the viewport; `render()` moves it up with `translateY` and clips it with `clip-path` to the element's box, at the offset set by the new `setScrollOffset`. Each canvas row has a state (invalid, joined with the next line, or cut), rows out of view are drawn when they come into view, and a viewport move past the overscan copies the rows with `shiftRows`. The last row in view and the row above the viewport are drawn without what the next line draws into them, as a full redraw of the viewport leaves its last row. Selection and regex link ranges are kept in canvas rows (the new `SelectionManager.getSelectionRange` is not clamped to the viewport), a hyperlink hover change repaints the rows out of view too, and the scrollbar repaints only the rows it no longer covers. `scrollOffset` and `visibleArea` are new getters; mouse hit testing in `terminal.ts` and `selection-manager.ts` subtracts `scrollOffset`. `resize()` in `terminal.ts` no longer sizes the element's backing store.
- `glide.ts`, `wheel.ts` (new), `terminal.ts`, `interfaces.ts`: wheel input to apps (ADR 045). `wheel.ts` holds the wheel helpers for apps: `wheelTicks`, `wheelSgr`, `wheelArrows` (on the alternate screen without mouse tracking, one arrow key per line of travel, keeping the remainder, instead of `round(deltaY / 33)` per event capped at 5) and `wheelArrowKey` (`ESC O A/B` under application cursor keys, which `less` sets), and `TickPacer`, which spreads an event's ticks over time at the `Pace` set through the new `attachWheelPace` instead of sending them in one burst. `glide.ts` is the motion both `TickPacer` and webtty's scrollback glide follow (`Glide`, `springStep`). The render loop calls the callback set by the new `attachBeforeRender` before it renders. Upstream's own eased normal-screen wheel scrolling (`smoothScrollTo`, `animateScroll`) and its `smoothScrollDuration` option are removed: webtty's custom wheel handler scrolls the normal screen, and that path left `viewportY` fractional.
- `interfaces.ts`, `types.ts`, `terminal.ts`, `ghostty.ts`: the `scrollbackLines` option (ADR 046). The terminal passes it in `GhosttyTerminalConfig.scrollbackLines`; the official engine then sets `SCROLLBACK_MAX_LINES` (NULL for 0) with `SCROLLBACK_MAX_BYTES` at 32 MiB instead of the derived byte limit. The Coder engine ignores it.
- `fn-table.ts`: not from ghostty-web. Copied unmodified (below its added header) from [gkoreli/ghostty-vt-js](https://github.com/gkoreli/ghostty-vt-js) at `248de81a188b71a1919d3c5c5bce2f99a836b5b1`, `packages/ghostty-vt-js/src/wasm/fn-table.ts`, MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 ghostty-vt-js contributors ([LICENSE.ghostty-vt-js](LICENSE.ghostty-vt-js)); `bun run build` adds the notice to `dist/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES`.
